title: Existing etale exceptional base change for open immersions
statement: Let Lambda be a finite commutative ring, and let g′ : X′ -> X, f′ : X′ -> Y′, f : X -> Y and g : Y′ -> Y be a Cartesian square of schemes. Suppose f and f′ are quasi-compact and admit compactifications, and g is an open immersion. The canonical ordinary etale derived exceptional base-change transformation Lg′* Rf! -> Rf′! Lg* is invertible. This is the existing source theorem named in the lean attachment, with no ambient pro-etale adjoint hypothesis.

proof.text: Use the two fully faithful derived open-extension adjunctions. The iterated-mate identity identifies the exceptional comparison with the conjugate of its inverse open mate gamma. On the target open, gamma is invertible because the open units and compact-support base-change transformation are invertible. On the closed complement both endpoints vanish: extension by zero restricts to zero, and compact-support base change identifies the other restriction with the extension from the disjoint pulled-back open. Open and closed restriction jointly reflect isomorphisms, so gamma is invertible. Its conjugate, the specified exceptional comparison, is invertible. The complete checked proof is the existing Lean declaration; this delivery only records it in the DAG.
